title: Harmonic dimension comparison in dimension three
exact_target: For every complete smooth metric g on $R^{3}$ with $Ric_g\geq 0$ and each integer $k\geq 0$, must the space of real harmonic functions of growth at most degree k have dimension $\leq (k+1)^{2}$, the Euclidean value? Each harmonic function may have its own growth constant.

sources.citation: OpenAI, manuscript citation page. Source of the formulation motivating this local problem.

families.title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
families.subject: Differential geometry

manuscripts.title: A Three-Dimensional Counterexample to Integer-Degree Harmonic Dimension Comparison
